body.statement:
Let a first-order formula over a real closed field have at most \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\) input polynomials of degree at most \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\), one block of \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}\) quantified variables, and one free variable.  It has an equivalent quantifier-free formula computable in
\[
s_{\mathrm{count}}^{\,2(p_{\mathrm{dim}}+1)}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}
\]
ring operations.  Its output polynomials have degree \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\).  For integer input coefficients of bit length at most \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\), all intermediate and output integer bit lengths are at most \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\).

source.locator: Theorem 2.27 and the preceding Block Elimination discussion, specialized to \(\omega=1\), \(k_1=p_{\mathrm{dim}}\), and \(\ell=1\)
source.verbatim_statement: Given Phi(Y), a (P,Pi)-formula, there exists an equivalent quantifier free formula. Complexity in D: s^{(k_omega+1)...(k_1+1)(ell+1)} d^{O(k_omega)...O(k_1)O(ell)}. Output degrees: d^{O(k_omega)...O(k_1)}. For integer coefficients of bit-size tau, intermediate and output bit-sizes are bounded by tau d^{O(k_omega)...O(k_1)O(ell)}.

upstream.citation: S. Basu, R. Pollack, and M.-F. Roy, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry, 2nd edition, Springer, 2006
upstream.locator: Cited as reference [25] by Basu survey Theorem 2.27 and Chapter 14 for Block Elimination

attestation.note: Checked against the official arXiv HTML for Basu, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry: A Survey, arXiv:1409.1534v1, Block Elimination discussion and Theorem 2.27 (lines 476-502), on 2026-09-11. Substituting omega=1, k_1=p_dim, ell=1 yields the core node bounds.
